response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability of PumpControl substates, reachable event-consumer coverage, and dead-end frontier facts. The closed FCSTM shows PumpControl has no outgoing transitions and no internal default entry connecting InitialState to PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState, so PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState and all their descendants are unreachable from root, InitialState is a reachable dead-end leaf, and every declared event consumer (Activate_Pump, Deactivate_Pump, Start_Monitoring, Stop_Monitoring) has zero reachable consumer transitions despite existing declared consumers. NL3's owner-local initial_entry contract (PumpControl -> PumpState) is refuted because the exact owner-local edge only targets InitialState, not PumpState, and PumpState itself has no inbound edge from PumpControl at all. NL4/NL5 endpoint contracts require PumpState->WaterState and PumpState->MethaneState transitions; the complete transition inventory contains no such edges (PumpState only reaches RunningState internally and has no outgoing transition to WaterState or MethaneState), so these are absent-edge (missing) facts even though the contracts label violation_direction as wrong_target — the complete-inventory-absence protocol requires an S2 candidate bound to the existing endpoint state refs. I also derive a reachability obligation for the PumpControl substates the NL text explicitly requires to be enterable/operable, and an event_consumer_coverage obligation reflecting that declared consumers for all four events are structurally unreachable from initial entry.

issues.reason: The complete-inventory absence protocol applies: both PumpState and MethaneState resolve to exact closed-model composite states, and the complete 8-row transition inventory contains no edge between them, so this is a direct missing-edge violation bound to the existing endpoint refs.
issues.requirement_quote: Similarly, the system can transition to the MethaneState substate, indicating that the pump is controlling or monitoring the methane flow.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue the concurrent-region structure inherently allows simultaneous activity in all three regions without an explicit transition, satisfying the intended behavior implicitly; but the contract requires an exact transition_endpoints edge, and concurrent co-activation is a distinct structural property that does not supply the required edge.
issues.title: No PumpState-to-MethaneState transition exists in the complete closed transition inventory

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions (transition:line:26 source=[*] target=InitialState, scope=PumpControl); exact_source_inventory tr_0002 (@initial:PumpControl -> InitialState); verify_facts proved_index initial-entry:transition:line:26 refers only to this edge, not to PumpState.
issues.expected: PumpControl's owner-local initial pseudostate edge should enter PumpState (or a state that leads into pump activation).
issues.observed: The only owner-local initial edge from PumpControl (transition:line:26 / source-tr_0002) targets InitialState, a leaf state with zero outgoing transitions. PumpState is a sibling composite with no inbound edge from PumpControl at all; it is only reached by its own internal pseudostate edge (transition:line:10, itself conditional/triggered).
issues.reason: The exact closed-model owner-local edge for PumpControl (line 26) targets InitialState exclusively; no edge from PumpControl or its initial pseudostate reaches PumpState. This directly refutes the owner-local initial_entry contract regardless of the separate root->PumpControl entry (NL1), which is a distinct scope.
issues.requirement_quote: The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue NL3's 'first transitions to PumpState' merely restates the general substate list from NL2 rather than imposing a strict owner-local edge; however NL3 explicitly separates this as the system's first transition, matching an initial_entry obligation on PumpControl distinct from NL2's containment claim.
issues.title: PumpControl owner-local initial entry targets InitialState, not PumpState

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions complete list (8 transitions, none PumpState->WaterState); exact_source_inventory.transitions (8 rows, none matching); fcstm_model.text showing PumpState only contains [*]->RunningState and RunningState->FinalWaittr_0004.
issues.expected: A transition edge from PumpState (or its operating state) to WaterState should exist in the closed model.
issues.observed: The complete FCSTM transition inventory (8 transitions) contains no edge with source in {PumpState, RunningState} and target in {WaterState, MonitoringWaterFlow}; PumpState's only outgoing edge is RunningState->FinalWaittr_0004 on Deactivate_Pump.
issues.reason: This is an exact absence in the complete closed transition inventory, not an ambiguous binding; per protocol this absence itself is candidate evidence bound to the two endpoint state refs.
issues.requirement_quote: The system can also transition to the WaterState substate, indicating that the pump is controlling or monitoring the water flow.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: WaterState and MethaneState are modeled as concurrent sibling regions under PumpControl rather than sequential targets from PumpState, so the NL's 'also transition to' may describe concurrent region entry rather than a literal PumpState->WaterState edge; still, no edge of any form connects PumpState's scope to WaterState.
issues.title: No PumpState-to-WaterState transition exists in the complete inventory

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions complete list (8 transitions, none PumpState->MethaneState); exact_source_inventory.transitions (8 rows, none matching); fcstm_model.text.
issues.expected: A transition edge from PumpState (or its operating state) to MethaneState should exist in the closed model.
issues.observed: The complete FCSTM transition inventory contains no edge with source in {PumpState, RunningState} and target in {MethaneState, MonitoringMethaneFlow}; PumpState's only outgoing edge targets FinalWaittr_0004 within its own scope.
issues.reason: Exact absence in the complete closed transition inventory; the endpoint state refs are bound as required since no such edge can supply its own ref.
issues.requirement_quote: Similarly, the system can transition to the MethaneState substate, indicating that the pump is controlling or monitoring the methane flow.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: As with WaterState, MethaneState is a concurrent sibling region under PumpControl, so the NL phrase may describe simultaneous region activity rather than a literal sequential edge; regardless, no edge of any kind links PumpState's scope to MethaneState in the closed model.
issues.title: No PumpState-to-MethaneState transition exists in the complete inventory

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.reachable_state_refs (only 3 of 12 states reachable); verify_facts non_proved reachability rows for PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState and their children; diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL (9 occurrences); fcstm_model.text PumpControl body showing only [*]->InitialState with no edge into PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState.
issues.expected: PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState, as PumpControl's core operating substates that the NL requires the system to actually enter and operate within (per NL1/NL3/NL4/NL5), should be reachable from the model root through PumpControl's default entry.
issues.observed: Deterministic reachable_state_refs are limited to {llms_emp_feedback_final_0002, PumpControl, InitialState}; verify_facts explicitly refutes reachability for PumpState, RunningState, FinalWaittr_0004, WaterState, MonitoringWaterFlow, FinalWaittr_0006, MethaneState, MonitoringMethaneFlow, FinalWaittr_0008 (9 states) because PumpControl's sole outgoing default edge goes only to the dead-end InitialState leaf, never into PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState.
issues.reason: This is a derived cross-view property: containment/cardinality contracts (NL2) are satisfied at the declaration level, but the NL's operational narrative (NL1, NL3-NL5) requires these substates to be actually entered, and the closed model's default-entry topology structurally isolates all three from root reachability. This is a distinct global reachability defect that individual owner-local initial_entry or endpoint contracts do not capture.
issues.requirement_quote: Within the PumpControl state, there are three main substates: PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: NL2 is a pure containment/declaration statement and could be read as not independently requiring reachability; however NL1/NL3/NL4/NL5 jointly establish that the system must actually operate within these substates, so root unreachability is a distinct behavioral defect beyond the satisfied containment/cardinality facts.
issues.title: PumpControl's three named operating substates are unreachable from root despite required containment/operation

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers (4 rows, reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] in all); verify_facts non_proved event_consumer rows for all 4 events; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE (4 occurrences).
issues.expected: Activate Pump/Deactivate Pump (governing PumpState per NL3) and Start/Stop Monitoring (governing WaterState/MethaneState per NL4/NL5) should each have at least one reachable consumer transition within PumpControl's operating scope, since the NL narrative requires the pump to actually be activated, controlled, and monitored.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers lists declared consumer_transition_refs for all four events (line:10, line:11, line:16/22, line:17/23) but reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty for every one; verify_facts explicitly refutes event-consumer reachability for Activate_Pump, Deactivate_Pump, Start_Monitoring, and Stop_Monitoring; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE confirm this for all four events.
issues.reason: This is a derived cross-view obligation: NL3/NL4/NL5 require the pump-activation and monitoring events to actually be operationally consumed, but the exact deterministic event-consumer facts show zero reachable consumers for every declared event, which is a distinct behavioral-coverage defect from bare declaration or from the composite-level reachability gap.
issues.requirement_quote: The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue this is fully subsumed by the PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState reachability defect already captured in the derived reachability contract; however consumer coverage is an independent operational property (a state could be reachable yet its event consumer transition still unreachable due to guard/trigger conditions), so it is preserved as its own distinct candidate per the lens's aggregation guidance.
issues.title: All four declared events have zero reachable consumers under PumpControl's required operating scope

An alternative concurrent_regions reading exists because the closed model documents three PlantUML concurrent regions under PumpControl, but the primary NL reading counts named substates, not region partitions.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability of PumpControl substates, reachable event-consumer coverage, and dead-end frontier facts. The closed FCSTM shows PumpControl has no outgoing transitions and no internal default entry connecting InitialState to PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState, so PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState and all their descendants are unreachable from root, InitialState is a reachable dead-end leaf, and every declared event consumer (Activate_Pump, Deactivate_Pump, Start_Monitoring, Stop_Monitoring) has zero reachable consumer transitions despite existing declared consumers. NL3's owner-local initial_entry contract (PumpControl -> PumpState) is refuted because the exact owner-local edge only targets InitialState, not PumpState, and PumpState itself has no inbound edge from PumpControl at all. NL4/NL5 endpoint contracts require PumpState->WaterState and PumpState->MethaneState transitions; the complete transition inventory contains no such edges (PumpState only reaches RunningState internally and has no outgoing transition to WaterState or MethaneState), so these are absent-edge (missing) facts even though the contracts label violation_direction as wrong_target — the complete-inventory-absence protocol requires an S2 candidate bound to the existing endpoint state refs. I also derive a reachability obligation for the PumpControl substates the NL text explicitly requires to be enterable/operable, and an event_consumer_coverage obligation reflecting that declared consumers for all four events are structurally unreachable from initial entry.

stage_receipts.reason: NL1 establishes root-level initial entry into PumpControl and broad capability context (not an endpoint). NL2 establishes containment of three named substates under PumpControl. NL3 establishes owner-local initial entry into PumpState from PumpControl (the 'first transitions' clause), and describes an activated/controlled pump condition, but does not state continuous/repeated action, so no state_action contract is manufactured. NL4 and NL5 establish sequential/alternative transition endpoints from PumpState to WaterState and PumpState to MethaneState (both introduced as coordinate 'also'/'similarly' alternatives from the same PumpState source, since NL1's broad-capability sentence does not fix a shared source and NL3 established PumpState as the current narrative point). These are captured as a shared-source transition group with two alternatives, plus individual endpoint contracts for each. No explicit guard or event is stated distinctly from the descriptive clauses, so no separate trigger/guard contracts are added; the descriptive clauses ('based on specific conditions', 'indicating that...') are treated as context, not exact formal guards. No termination, cardinality-domain, or region-structure obligation is explicitly stated beyond the direct_child_states count of three substates under PumpControl (NL2), captured as a cardinality contract. No explicit continuous/repeated activity phrasing is present, so no state_action contracts are added.
